memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make a lampstand of pure gold. Hammer out its base and shaft, and make its flowerlike cups, buds and blossoms of one piece with them. Six branches are to extend from the sides of the lampstand — three on one side and three on the other. Three cups shaped like almond flowers with buds and blossoms are to be on one branch, three on the next branch, and the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand." - Exodus 25:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The lampstand was a work of extraordinary beauty — gold hammered into the shape of a flowering almond tree, with branches, buds, and blossoms. And crucially, it was all of one piece. Not assembled from parts joined together, but beaten patiently from a single mass of gold until the beauty emerged. That took time, skill, and countless blows of the hammer.

There is something quietly profound in that. Beauty came through hammering. The craftsman did not pour the gold into a mould for a quick result; he shaped it slowly, strike by strike, until the design appeared. God often works the same way in us. The shaping is not always gentle, and it is rarely fast, but the goal is beauty He can see before we can.

If you are in a season that feels like hammering, take heart. God is not being careless with you. Scripture says that suffering produces perseverance, character, and hope (Rom 5:3-4), and that God is conforming us to the image of His Son (Rom 8:29). Nothing is wasted in His hands. The blows that feel like damage may be the very strokes forming something lovely. Trust the Craftsman with the hammer.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I in a season of "hammering" where God may be shaping something beautiful?
Can I trust the Craftsman even when His shaping is uncomfortable?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are shaping me with skill and purpose, even when it feels like hammering. Help me trust Your hands and believe You are forming something beautiful in me. Amen.
